The kerb is at y about 383, and his feet are at (281,386) at 249.2 and (279,392) at 249.6. He then walks down to the west zebra. That short step does not meet the jaywalking definition, and the claimed positions are wrong. From 250.2 his legs are hidden behind the woman in beige who is standing still at (272,448), so the "(273,405) at 251.0" point is a cut-off box bottom (box height drops from 60 to 40). If you add his full height of 60 to 62 px to the head top, which stays visible, his feet are at (275,399) at 250.0, (273,406) at 250.4, (274,412) at 250.8 and (274,416) at 251.2. His perpendicular distance outside the bright stripe edge is then 25, 13, 6, 1 and 0 px, so he is on the stripes by about 250.8, not 251.4. He is more than about a body width outside (box width is about 20 px) only from 249.2 to about 249.7. Also, the gap between the island and the bright stripes is not bare road: worn white and yellow stripe paint continues the bright stripes up to about 5 px below the island kerb (seen on the empty frame at 240.0). He is on or at the edge of that worn paint from about 249.8. So this is a step of under 2 s from the island onto the crossing edge, not a walk in the road outside the crossing. Unsure, so rejected. For context only (not this claim): the clear off-crossing stretch for S-b was earlier. He came off the north crossing near (335,318) at about 244.0 and crossed about 20 px of junction-box asphalt to the island apex at about 245.9, then walked along the island until 249.2. Those times are rough and not pinned to 0.1 s. C3902.label: stopped_vehicle
C3902.reason: The physical claim holds. The black SUV swings round from the junction box and heads north. Its brake lights come on at 88.8, and it stands with its nose at the south edge of the NB zebra, at proxy about (800,280). It moves at most a couple of px until it creeps off at about 106.2-106.4 and turns into NB by 107.2. But the frames show why it stood there. At 88.8-89.6 a man in a white shirt walks across the NB zebra directly in front of its bumper. From about 92 to 106 groups of pedestrians keep crossing that zebra in its path during their walk phase (the avenue signal is red). From about 98 the east-arm right-turners (black SUVs) pull up beside and behind it and wait at the same crossing. The white SUV ahead-right also waits there until about 99. The SUV leaves as soon as the pedestrian flow thins. So this is a vehicle yielding to pedestrians at the head of a queue at the crossing: ordinary turning traffic held by the pedestrian phase, the same thing as a signal queue. It is not an abnormal stop (not broken down, not dropping off passengers, not standing in the box for no reason). The labeller flagged low confidence, and the guide says to reject when unsure. No other class fits the standing: it waited rather than driving across the zebra, so it is not failure_to_yield, and stop_line applies only to SB vehicles at the SB stop line. Any U-turn or red-light question about how it got there is a separate event.

C3902.label: jaywalking
C3902.reason: The left man in the white T-shirt is really there, but he walks along the east edge of the west zebra, not beside it. The labeller's measurement is a perspective error. From 127.3 to 129.5 only his head and torso are in frame, and his feet are about 15 to 70 proxy px below the bottom edge. The labeller compared his torso x to where the stripes end at the frame edge (y about 540). I measured the stripe ends on an empty frame (126.9 s) and they fall on a line of about x = y - 122 (proxy), for example (349,472), (384,508) and (413,535). Where his feet are visible, from 130.2 s on, he is about 75 px tall. Placing his feet 75 px below his head gives: 127.4 feet about (493,609) against a stripe edge of 487; 128.0 (473,595) against 473; 128.8 (450,573) against 451; 129.8 (419,554) against 432. So he is 0 to 6 px (at most about a quarter of a body width) outside the stripe line, and by 129.8 he is already inside it. Once his feet show up he is plainly on the zebra's edge stripes: at 130.2 his feet are at x 402-412 with the edge at 415, at 130.6 x 390-400 with the edge at 410, and at 131.0 and 131.4 he is inside the stripes. He is never more than about a body width outside, so this is not jaywalking under labeling.md. The avenue signal is green, so the west-crossing walk phase is running and the crossing is legal. No other class fits: no vehicle crosses the west zebra near him in this window. Side note, not the claimed actor: his companion on the right (also in a white T-shirt) walks roughly one body width (20 to 35 px) east of the stripe line from about 128.0 to 131.4 and joins the edge by about 132.2. That is borderline, and I would not label it without its own review. Sheets are in out/sheets/refute_C3902_jw127/ (grid_a, grid_b and grid_c have a proxy-px grid and the fitted stripe-edge line).
